newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan firms flock to Singapore in hope of listing.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan firms flock to Singapore in hope of listing.

text.p: Taiwanese firms, aiming for a listing on Singapore's stock market, have boosted their inward investment to the country by about 200 percent in the first nine months of 1996, the Business Times newspaper said on Monday.

"Most of the new investment is by holding companies setting up regional headquarters in Singapore in the hope of an eventual listing on the local stock market," Huang Chin-tan, vice-executive secretary of the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs was quoted as saying.
Investment Commission figures reported in the newspaper show Taiwan made investments of US$100 million in Singapore in the year to September against $31.6 million in the same period of 1995.
About eight small and medium-sized Taiwan companies are thought to be interested in expanding regional operations via a Singapore listing.
Although total investment is comparatively small -- $392 million in 153 projects -- the newspaper said analysts consider the inward trend significant.

Taiwan invested a total of $4.17 billion in the first nine months of 1996 in Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam and Singapore, a rise of 55 per cent over the previous year, said the report.
